title: IMMEDIATELY.
paragraphs:
No meeting.
No seminar.
No five-year plan.
And fishermen walked away from everything.
The shoreline of Sea of Galilee was alive that morning.

Nets dripping.
Calloused hands pulling rope.
Fish scales glinting in the sun.
This was ordinary life for Simon Peter and his brother Andrew.
Then a rabbi from Nazareth stepped into their story.
Jesus Christ looked at them and said:
“Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men.” — Gospel of Matthew 4:19
And the next verse explodes with a word that still shakes history:
Further down the shore, two more brothers were repairing gear with their father.

James son of Zebedee.
John the Apostle.

They left the boat.
They left the nets.
They even left their father.
But because a greater call had arrived.

We like Jesus…
but we like our nets too.

The job.
The comfort zone.
The habits we know.
But the kingdom often moves at the speed of obedience.
Here’s the grace hidden inside this moment.
Jesus did not call perfect men.

These fishermen would misunderstand Him.
Argue about greatness.
Run away when the cross came.
Because discipleship doesn’t begin with perfection.

Every one of us is tangled in deeper nets—
nets of sin, fear, pride, and self-rule.
But Jesus stepped into our shoreline.

At the cross, He carried our sin.
At the empty tomb, He shattered death.
Sometimes destiny starts with a simple yes.
And watch ordinary lives become part of an eternal story.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
